decisions.reason: Changing the 5V_EN GPIO does not alter the DCDC1 3.3V rail voltage, rating, or load role.
The GPIO reassignment does not change the AXP2101 battery input or normal system power path.
The charge-status interfaces and their GPIO13, CHGLED, D1, and R6 details are unaffected.
The source changes controller GPIO assignments, not the battery connector or its unresolved pin order.
The battery-protection controller, thresholds, and protection components remain unchanged.
The NTC connector and AXP2101 thermal-monitoring behavior are unaffected by the GPIO changes.
The current LED standby-power rule explicitly assigns shared 5V-rail control to GPIO3, so the client's reassignment of 5V_EN to GPIO5 necessarily updates that rule.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, GPIO3 was from my original ESP32 design — mistake on my side. For 5V_EN you can use GPIO5. Also I realized GPIO22, 23, 25, 27 are not exposed on the WROOM-1 module, so I need to reassign SCL0 (GPIO22→38), SPI MOSI (GPIO23→26). I'll update the docs and send you the full updated GPIO table.

value_updates.standby_power_control: Switch off the shared 5V rail through 5V_EN controlled by GPIO5 when the LEDs are not needed

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording 5V_EN on GPIO5, SCL0 on GPIO38, and SPI MOSI on GPIO26.
The connector pinout exposes the symbolic 5V_EN and SCL0 signals rather than their ESP32 GPIO assignments, so it remains valid unchanged.
Controller GPIO reassignment does not affect the power board's four-layer stack.
The standalone USB 3.3V supply path and source-selection behavior do not depend on the reassigned 5V_EN, SCL0, or SPI MOSI GPIOs.
The GPIO changes do not alter the number or functional separation of project boards.
